$comment: Desk grade (not hands-on). Steam review quotes come from the English review JSON (filter=all, 4 pages, 124 unique reviews sampled, 80% up); review ids given.
build: Steam app 1267910 as of 2026-10-15 (base + 3 expansions; latest Steam news 2025-04-23 'Melvor Idle 2 - Coming Soon to Steam Early Access'; Offline Client beta 2024-11-19)

package.basis: desk: Steam store data and review API (9,398 English reviews, 92% positive, Very Positive), the Melvor wiki Offline Progression page, Steam news, a vaporlens review aggregate and prior repo research; not played.

fun.source: eval/calibration/melvor-idle.scorecard.json (65.4 on idle-rpg preset, gated on surprise); carried over to idle-hybrid unchanged

evidence.quote: Master Melvor's many RuneScape-style skills with just a click or a tap.
it's basically OSRS without the 3d graphics
visually bland, with minimal animations

dims.note: RuneScape-style item icons on a dense web dashboard; readable, not distinctive. Slightly under the rubric's 50 anchor because reviews call it bland.

evidence.quote: it's literally OSRS with no animations
minimal animations

dims.note: Progress bars and combat HP bars; matches the rubric's ~20 anchor.

evidence.quote: Well laid out and intuitive.
the UI is horrible, it bombards you with like 30 mechanics right at the get go
a spreadsheet-like interface

dims.note: Split opinion: clean once learned, dense sidebar at the start. Wiki leaned on (review 237564083: 'read the wiki page for each skill').

evidence.quote: The lack of music or other sounds make it less useful as a study tool
no sound effects

dims.note: Graded from review consensus, not listened. Reviews describe it as essentially silent; the rubric's 50 anchor for Melvor audio looks wrong (it misses by >15 points, so per §5 the anchor text should be revised).

evidence.quote: it has a great tutorial to understand the basics
Quick start, many simultaneous characters ... Lots of information to take in at first though.
Auto Eat I costs 1M GP; 'upgrading this as quickly as possible is critical' (via docs/research/PROGRESSION_COMPETITORS_2026-10.md §1)

dims.note: Core act (pick a skill) in seconds; first real combat automation (Auto Eat) is a large gold sink hours in. Matches the 50 anchor.

evidence.quote: even after a few weeks, I'm nowhere near to unlocking them
tons of easter eggs and new things to find after hundreds of hours
Excessively slow progression

dims.note: Many skills give parallel goals so there is always a next level; long, mostly visible grinds (level 99 curves). No ending; completion log is a months-long target.

evidence.quote: Every skill in this game serves a purpose, interacting with the others in interesting ways.
It's got a TON of depth to it.
there doesn't seem to be a wrong way to go about it

dims.note: Gear sets, combat styles, prayers, summoning synergies and skill interplay; but few forks matter (no wrong way), and no scripting layer.

evidence.quote: progress while closed as if the player had remained online ... (up to a maximum of 24 hours)
$9.99, three paid expansion DLCs, no In-App Purchases category
if I don't have an internet connection the game won't launch

dims.note: Exact offline sim and one-price model; lapses: 24 h cap and an online requirement (an Offline Client has been in beta since 2024-11). No paid time skips found.

evidence.quote: visually bland, with minimal animations
if you get dopamine hits from seein[g numbers go up]

dims.note: Toasts and level-up notices; reward is the number itself. Below the 50 anchor given no sound and few effects.

evidence.quote: it's well-made, well-designed, and runs well
having a bug that prevents the game from closing
Cloud saves being broken ruined all progression

dims.note: Long-lived and generally stable; recent negatives cluster on cloud/server outages and Steam client close/startup bugs. Under the rubric's 80 anchor for that reason.

evidence.quote: over 20 skills ... face off against 100+ monsters; three expansion DLCs listed
Great idle game with a ton of content and expansions
only buy TOH DLC, other 2 are ... copy&paste content

dims.note: Matches the rubric's 80 benchmark (itself); lapse: later expansions called reskins by some.

evidence.quote: Inspired by RuneScape ... Maxing 20+ skills has never been more zen.
it's like Runescape except I don't have to actually sit at my PC for 12 hours

dims.note: Instantly legible pitch, but borrowed from RuneScape; screenshot shows a dashboard.

evidence.quote: Windows, Mac, Linux; 13 interface languages incl. Japanese, Korean, Russian, Chinese
a version on steam, a phone app, and browser with cloud syncing
Single player idle game that requires connection to server.

dims.note: Web, Steam, iOS/Android with cross-save; no evidence found either way on text scaling or reduced-motion settings.

learn.practice: Simulate absence exactly as if online and say so plainly; players trust offline only when it matches online.
learn.evidence: https://wiki.melvoridle.com/w/Offline_Progression — 'There is no actual difference between being Online and being Offline when it comes to getting items/experience'

learn.practice: One save everywhere: the same run on browser and phone with cloud sync lets a player glance from either device.
learn.evidence: https://store.steampowered.com/appreviews/1267910 (review 231131734) — 'a version on steam, a phone app, and browser with cloud syncing'

learn.practice: Make every system feed another (town buildings feed the climb, the climb feeds the town) so no upgrade is a dead end.
learn.evidence: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1267910 — 'Every skill in this game serves a purpose, interacting with the others in interesting ways.'

learn.practice: Never require a connection for a single-player idler; the online requirement is Melvor's most cited recent complaint.
learn.evidence: https://store.steampowered.com/appreviews/1267910 (review 237393303) — 'if I don't have an internet connection the game won't launch'
